lines: The reset email is in your inbox. One tap, and you choose a new password.
The link opens the Reset password screen. It checks the link first, then names the account it belongs to.
The link's secret sits after the hash sign, so no server ever logs it. The screen reads it, then wipes it from the address bar.
Type the new password twice and press save. The button says, saving, then your password is saved.
Saving signs you out on every device, this one too. You sign in again with the new password.
A link works once, for thirty minutes. Used, expired or unknown, it shows the same page, with a new link one tap away.
Passwords that don't match, or are too short, are named before anything is sent.
If the server fails, a message says so, and both passwords stay, ready to try again.
Even two saves at the same moment can't use one link twice. The second is refused.
Every test failed first. Now they all pass.
That's slice twenty point two, and journey twenty is done. Christian Fitness: a Christian community for health in body and spirit.
